p.i: α.1. ἡξα. P. ἦχα Attice ἀγῆχα & per epenthe-fin ἔ ο μιzῷ ἀγήοχα. α.2. ἦγὴν Attice ἠγαγὴν. α.2. imperat. ἄγαγε, ἀγάγετε. subj. α.2. ἀγά-γωμεν ἡ. 3.pl. ἀγάγωσιν. infin. α.2. ἀγαγεῖν. part. α.2. ἀγαγὼν. prꝏat. pass. ἠγμαι. α.1. pass. ἤχθλη. α.1. pass. infin. ἀχθλῶις, Act.5.21. fut.1. pass. ἀχθήσομαι, Matth.10.18.

main_text.p: ᾽Αγὼν ὢν& ὁ certamen, 1.Tim.6.12. item stadium, sive locus in quæ curritur, Heb.12.1.
᾽Αγωνίζομαι certo, enitor, Luc.13.24. imperf. ἠγωνιζόμην & ἐ͏ῷ. F.1.med. ἀγωνίσομαι. P.pass. ἠγώνισμαι certavi.

᾽Αδελφὸς ὃ ὁ frater (ex α quod est ex ἀμφω simul, & ἀδελφὺς ὁ& ἡ uterus) cognatus, consanguineus, Matth.12.46. christianus, proximus, popularis, hoc est, ejusdem populi membrum, & opponitur peregrino, Luc.17.3.
᾽Αδελφὴ ης ἡ soror, christiana, uxor, cognata, 1.Cor.9.5.
᾽Αδηλος ὁ ἡ non apparens, incertus. ex α priv. & δηλος ἡ ον manifestus, 1.Cor.14.8.
᾽Αδήλως adv. proprie obscure. non manifeste, item in incertum, 1.Cor.9.26.
᾽Αδημονέω ῶ gravissimè angor, pene exanimor. F. ήσω. P. ἠδημόνηκα. α.1. ἠδημόνησα, Matth.26.37.

page.notes: The facing page at the far right edge is cropped; only fragments of its marginal notes are visible (Greek and Latin reference fragments such as "Luc.16.", "Matth.", "1.Pet.2.2", "1.Cor." and "Act." in small type) and are not transcribed in full. The running head is set in Greek capitals and was read as ΑΓΑΔ; the letters are spaced and may differ slightly. Greek forms, accents and breathings in the entries are uncertain in several places and should be checked against the scan.
